problems.detail: robots.txt Sitemap line points at http://localhost:3000/sitemap.xml — placeholder base; if deployed as-is, crawlers get a dead sitemap URL. Must be swapped to the live domain at push time (same localhost-base issue as sitemap/llms/canonicals).
all 31 sitemap locs use http://localhost:3000 base — placeholder; must be swapped to the live domain at push time or the sitemap is useless live.
llms.txt URLs use http://localhost:3000 base — same placeholder-base note as sitemap; swap at push time.

Legal pages have bare, very short titles verbatim from the doc — Disclaimer (10ch), Terms of Use (12ch), Privacy Policy (14ch) — with no brand/location. Titles MATCH pages-data.json exactly, so this is an observation only, not a mismatch; changing them would break the verbatim rule. Terms of Use description is also short (47ch). Flagging for coordinator decision, not a fix.

notes: Built HTML == rendered DOM for meta/robots/canonical: this is a static Next.js export (no client JS rewrites head tags). Meta robots/canonical/title/description were read from the served built HTML, which is exactly what a crawler receives.

pages-data.json 'url' field carries trailing-slash forms (/about/) but the canonical/sitemap/llms URL form used by the build is no-trailing-slash; the audit compared against the built (no-slash) form per the task spec.

FAQ questions render as H3 in the built HTML and are already present in the blocks h3 list (verified: faq set is a subset of blocks h3 on every page checked); the H3 comparison uses blocks h3 only to avoid double-counting.
